newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein stable in thin late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein stable in thin late trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were mostly stable in late trading on Friday as buying interest remained thin amid a lack of fresh factors, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,375-80 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but trades were also heard at 5-10 rupiah below and above the range. Crude palm oil was last done at around 1,175 rupiah/kg in Medan on Wednesday.

"Sentiment is still weak despite a turnaround in Malaysia," one trader said. "Players are not keen on taking fresh positions because of the weakening market, preferring instead to wait and see price developments."
"The situation has not been helped any by some players selling well below the market range," he said. "One seller was quoting 1,360 rupiah/kg for purchases of 500 tonnes."

The traders said they expected prices to remain weak next week on the back of poor demand and as players waited for official Malaysian crop data from the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA).
"I think the PORLA report will give some direction on where prices will head," one trader said. "Malaysia's production and export levels will be the key."

Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Petrobulk Jaguar will head for Rotterdam on Sunday with 15,520 tonnes of crude palm oil. The MT Stolt Protector will leave for Singapore on Saturday with 12,000 tonnes of coconut oil.
The Herefordshire will leave on Saturday for Bangkok with 3,100 tonnes of crude palm oil.
